User profile information

Typically private data, not to be retrieved by any user

registered_via.description: How the account was created (e.g. 'invitation'); null for seeded/legacy/unknown

cohort_hash.description:
Advisory device-cohort hash (slice `S-C13`), the client-asserted grouping aid from
[Authentication — Device Cohorts]. Optional and **unverifiable**: it is stored to group
this device's sessions and is never read by any authorization decision — absent or
garbage values are accepted and behave identically to a valid one.

[Authentication — Device Cohorts]: https://docs/design/authentication/#device-cohorts

device_id.description:
The directory `device_id` (a UUID) this session is opened from (slice `S-N3`).
Optional; recorded so the session listing can emit the support bundle's
`(device_id, session_id)` pairs. A malformed value is treated as absent, and — like
the cohort — nothing here gates authorization.

auth.models.responses.Device.description:
One active session in the session listing (slice `S-C13`), carrying **both** identifiers
the support bundle needs (slice `S-N3`).

[`Device::id`] is the *session* id and [`Device::device_id`] is the *device* id — two
distinct identifier spaces that must both be present, because a support report pairs them
(`{cohort_hash, [(device_id, session_id, first_seen, last_seen)]}`) and one physical
device accumulates several session ids over its life.

cohort_hash.description:
The advisory device-cohort hash asserted when this session was created (slice
`S-C13`), or `None` if the client did not assert one. A grouping aid only — clients
group the ledger by this value; it carries no authority.

device_id.description:
The **device** id this session was opened from (slice `S-N3`): the UUID naming an
entry in the user's device directory, as asserted by the client at session creation,
or `None` when it asserted none. Paired with `id` this yields the support bundle's
`(device_id, session_id)` rows. Client-asserted and therefore never an authorization
input.

id.description:
The **session** id. Historically the only identifier on this surface; it keeps its
name so existing clients keep deserializing, and `device_id` is added beside it rather
than renaming this field into something it is not.

auth.models.responses.DeviceCohort.description:
One entry of the durable device-cohort map surfaced alongside the session listing (slice
`S-C13`). Lets a client label a cohort "a device you've used before (last seen …)" even
when its earlier sessions have expired — the map outlives sessions.

cohort_hash.description: The advisory cohort hash (opaque; the client groups its sessions by this).

first_seen.description: First time this cohort was seen for the user (Unix seconds).

last_seen.description: Most recent time this cohort was seen for the user (Unix seconds).

auth.models.responses.SessionListingResp.description:
The session-listing surface (slice `S-C13`): the user's active sessions, each carrying its
advisory cohort, plus the durable cohort map. Clients group the ledger by cohort.

cohorts.description: The durable cohort map (persists beyond session expiry).

devices.description: Active sessions ("devices"), each annotated with its per-session cohort.

auth.routes.devices.ChannelResponse.description: The established relay channel handle the ceremony continues over.

channel_id.description: Opaque relay-channel handle for the ephemeral-ECDH ceremony messages.

auth.routes.devices.EnrollmentCodeRespon.description:
The issued enrollment code, displayed as a QR (full entropy) with a shorter,
rate-limited numeric text fallback.

code.description: The full-entropy code for the QR payload (URL-safe base64; ≥64 bits).

text_fallback.description:
The shorter transcribable fallback (safe because redemption is single-use,
expiring, and rate-limited; channel integrity rests on the safety code).

auth.routes.devices.RedeemRequest.description: A redemption request from the new device.

code.description: The scanned or typed enrollment code (either the QR form or the numeric fallback).

auth.routes.devices.RelayMessagesRespons.description: The drained opaque payloads pending in a channel mailbox.

messages.description: Payloads in arrival order; the mailbox is drained on read.

auth.routes.devices.RelaySendRequest.description: A request to relay one opaque ceremony payload into a channel mailbox.

payload.description: The opaque payload, relayed verbatim — the server never decodes it.

to.description:
Target mailbox: `"a"` toward the initiator (device A), `"b"` toward the enrollee
(device B).

auth.routes.directory.PublishDirectoryRe.description: The accepted-version acknowledgement for a successful publish.

directory_version.description: The `directory_version` now stored for the user (equals the submitted version).

auth.routes.revoke.RevokeAllChallengeRes.description: A freshly issued revoke-all challenge for the client to sign with its identity key.

challenge.description:
The opaque challenge. The client signs the domain-separated canonical-CBOR encoding of
`(domain, user_id, challenge)` over this exact string and echoes it back in the proof.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 expiry. Single-use: it is spent by the first proof presented against it.

user_id.description:
The account the challenge is bound to, echoed because it is folded into the signed
bytes. It is the caller's own id (the access token's `sub`) — returned so a client
never has to crack open a JWT to build the signing input, and so a mismatch is caught
before signing rather than as an opaque refusal.

auth.routes.revoke.RevokeAllResponse.description: The acknowledgement for a completed global revoke.

revoked_sessions.description: How many sessions were invalidated, the calling session included.

media.routes.receipts.AssetReceipt.description: One custody receipt, decoded, plus its signed CBOR form.

envelope_hash.description: SHA-256 of the manifest envelope CBOR (hex), when present.

prior_receipt_hash.description: SHA-256 of the previous receipt (hex), absent for the first receipt.

receipt_cbor.description: The full signed receipt as canonical CBOR (base64).

received_at.description: The server's trusted clock at the finalization commit (RFC 3339).

server_key_id.description: The attestation key fingerprint that signed (hex).

upload_id.description: The upload session that produced custody.

receipts.description: Every receipt covering the asset, in chain order.

media.routes.verify.AssetVerifyRequest.description: One asset to verify: the exact blob hashes the client is relying on.

blob_hashes.description: Content addresses (hex) of every blob the client relies on.

indexed.description: Referenced by a committed, `uploaded = true` row.

role.description:
`original | metadata | derivative | provenance` — or `unknown` for a hash the server
does not associate with the asset.

stored.description: Present in the blob store at its content address.

blobs.description:
Per-blob detail, one entry per declared hash (a hash the server does not associate
with the asset comes back `stored=false, indexed=false` — never silently omitted).

checked_at.description: The server's trusted clock at verification (RFC 3339).

durable.description: All required blobs stored ∧ indexed ∧ retrievable.

deep.description:
Re-read and re-hash blob bytes instead of trusting stat + index (rate-limited and
coalesced server-side).

nonce.description:
An optional client freshness challenge (base64), echoed verbatim into every signed
attestation so a stale `durable = true` cannot be replayed as current. Ignored unless
`signed`.

signed.description:
Return a server-signed [`StorageAttestation`] per asset instead of the bare verdict —
evidence a client can retain. Server-priced like `deep` (rate-limited per user).

upload.models.responses.CreateUploadResp.description: Response for a successful upload creation

suggested_chunk_size.description: Suggested chunk size for this upload

upload_url.description: URL to use for uploading chunks

upload.models.responses.QuotaResponse.description: Response for `GET /quota` — the uploader's storage-quota snapshot (S-C6).

hard_limit.description: Hard-refusal threshold in bytes (`null` when unlimited).

soft_limit.description: Soft-warning threshold in bytes (`null` when unlimited).

state.description: Quota state: `ok | soft_warning | hard_exceeded | grace_expired | suspended`.

used.description: Bytes currently charged to the uploader.

upload.models.session.BlobRole.description:
The blob's role within its asset bundle, declared at session creation and
recorded on the pending row (closed enum; the visibility gate and staged
uploads reason over it — see the upload-protocol design doc).

upload.models.session.UploadSession.description:
Volatile transfer state for one upload session.

The record carries everything finalization needs — sizes, hash, crypto/protocol
pins, blob role, the manifest envelope, and the parties — so a session is
finalizable from its own record with no further client input (upload-protocol
design doc, §Endpoints).

album_id.description: Optional Album ID to link the upload to

asset_id.description: Asset ID (usually created by Postgres during session creation)

content_type.description: Content type of the file being uploaded

crypto_suite_id.description:
Crypto suite the blob was sealed under (validated against the inventory by
the envelope gate, S-C1)

expected_hash.description: Expected SHA-256 hash for verification on finalize (64-char lowercase hex)

intent_id.description: Album-upgrade intent, when part of an upgrade ceremony

last_progress_at.description:
Timestamp of the last accepted chunk (creation time if none). Anchors the
≥1-hour survival floor; the pressure sweeper (S-C1) evicts
least-recently-progressed first.

manifest_envelope.description:
The server-visible manifest envelope, serialized JSON. Stored opaquely on
the session; deep validation is the envelope gate's job (S-C1).

protocol_version.description: Pinned protocol date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) from session creation

upload_user_id.description: User ID who initiated the upload (this matters for storage quota)

upload.routes.receipt.ReceiptResponse.description: The decoded receipt view returned alongside the signed CBOR.

envelope_hash.description: SHA-256 of the manifest envelope CBOR (hex), when present.

prior_receipt_hash.description: SHA-256 of the previous receipt (hex), absent for the first receipt.

receipt_cbor.description: The full signed receipt as canonical CBOR (base64) — verify under the attestation key.

received_at.description: The server's trusted clock at the finalization commit (RFC 3339).

server_key_id.description: The attestation key fingerprint that signed (hex).
